content: If you are allergic to this medication, polyethylene glycol (PEG), or have any other allergies, inform your doctor or pharmacist before using it. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication can increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Notify your healthcare provider that you are using peginterferon alfa-2a before receiving any vaccinations or immunizations. This drug may cause dizziness, which can be exacerbated by alcohol or marijuana (cannabis). Refrain from driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Avoid consuming alcoholic beverages. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, particularly mental or mood changes such as severe depression or suicidal thoughts/attempts. Peginterferon alfa-2a may also slow a child’s growth, potentially resulting in a lower-than-expected final adult height. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using peginterferon alfa-2a, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss reliable birth control options with your healthcare provider while on this medication. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests, such as blood counts, thyroid tests, virus levels, kidney/liver function, triglyceride levels, and eye exams, should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically during treatment. Do not switch brands of interferon without consulting your doctor or pharmacist. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember, provided it is within two days of the scheduled dose. Administer your next dose on your usual dosing day. Store this medication in the refrigerator, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it or leave it out of the refrigerator for more than 24 hours. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Most people experience flu-like symptoms, such as headache, fatigue, fever, chills, and muscle aches, which typically decrease after the first few weeks of treatment. To minimize these side effects, inject the medication at bedtime and use fever reducers or pain relievers like acetaminophen before each dose. Other side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dry mouth, loss of appetite, dizziness, trouble sleeping, or redness/swelling at the injection site. Tooth and gum problems may also occur, especially if dry mouth persists. Prevent dry mouth by drinking plenty of water or using a saliva substitute. Brush your teeth thoroughly at least twice daily and schedule regular dental exams. Temporary hair loss may also occur. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, it may cause serious mental or mood changes, which could worsen during treatment or after your last dose. Additionally, this drug may weaken your immune system, increasing the risk of serious (rarely fatal) infections or worsening existing infections. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor for medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
